body.statement: Construct and characterize an evaluated representation implementing \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{mom}}\) such that every cutoff-forest message remains closed under arbitrary heterogeneous branching, forest-component products, moving endpoints at ordered core priorities, and zero-, one-, and two-tagged coefficient extraction, while its state count, arithmetic count, and intermediate rational bit height are each bounded by \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\). The representation must match exact residual enumeration on every \(\Gamma_{k,m,M}\) instance with \(k\le3\), \(m\le2\), branch weights in \(\{1,2\}\), and all admissible tags, and it must have a symbolic arbitrary-\(k,m\) complexity proof.
body.justification: This is the isolated open question separating the proved dense XP algorithm from arbitrary-feedback-set fixed-parameter tractability.
body.gap: Heterogeneous branches preserve distinct future ordered-ratio exponent profiles, and no state algebra of fixed-parameter size is proved to close them.
body.consumer: A future solution would sharpen the general XP bound; no current design recommendation relies on that sharpening.

obligation.what_is_open: Whether an evaluated representation with state count and bit complexity \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) is closed under arbitrary heterogeneous cutoff-forest branching, component multiplication, moving ordered-core endpoints, and all zero-, one-, and two-tag coefficient extractions remains open.
obligation.obstruction: On an ordered chamber, a heterogeneous component with branch exponents \(a_{ji}\) and center weight \(c_j\) has nonconstant cutoff terms carrying the future profile \((c_j+A_{jr},\ldots,c_j+A_{jk})\), where \(A_{jr}=\sum_{i\le r}a_{ji}\).  For \(k=2\), profiles \((1,1)\) and \((1,2)\) produce \(T_{11}=1/3+(t_1^2/2+1/6)t_2^3\) and \(T_{12}=1/4+(t_1^2/2+1/4)t_2^4\).  Activating the \(t_1\)-dependent term in either factor leaves the same current exponent but different future exponents.  Thus relative core order, a scalar activation count, and a current-degree total are not closed states; retaining all \(k\) degree totals gives the forbidden \((nb)^{\Theta(k)}\) behavior.
obligation.attempted: The three-state recursion and \(3^k\) inclusion--exclusion were reduced to chamber polynomials; the vertex-cover case was evaluated monomial by monomial; and identical replicated-star attachments were compressed by the one-index nested-moment recurrence.  The same recurrence was expanded for the two heterogeneous profiles above, where it fails because the future exponents differ.  Dense chamber-polynomial evaluation does close all operations but has \((nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\) rather than fixed-parameter dependence.
obligation.partial_result: The proved partial result is a complete evaluated XP algorithm for arbitrary feedback forests with cost \(Ln^2k!3^k(nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\), together with a \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) vertex-cover oracle and an \(O(k!km^2)\)-operation recurrence for identical replicated-star attachments.  These results contain no unevaluated integration gate, but they do not provide the requested general heterogeneous FPT closure.
